Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: The plan provides a comprehensive district-wide inventory including building ages, sizes, types, and detailed site plans for all schools and facilities (Sections 3, pages 17-50). It includes robust condition assessments covering major systems (HVAC, roofing, electrical, plumbing) with detailed findings and recommendations (Sections 3, pages 33-35, 40-45). The plan connects facility conditions to student outcomes and instructional priorities, and integrates short- and long-term needs into capital planning.

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: The plan includes a comprehensive enrollment analysis with detailed methodology covering demographic trends, birth rates, migration, and housing development (Section 5, pages 61-75). It provides detailed capacity utilization data by site and classroom, including permanent and portable capacities (Section 5, pages 76-79). The plan explicitly links enrollment projections to facility actions and discusses strategies for consolidation and adaptive uses.

Educational Alignment.justification: The plan includes a section on educational standards and suitability, linking educational goals to facility assessments and improvements (Section 2, pages 13-19). It discusses educational specifications such as flexible classrooms, technology integration, and specialized spaces. However, connections between facility projects and specific educational programs are present but not fully comprehensive or deeply integrated.

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: The plan references outdoor spaces such as play areas, athletic fields, and shade structures at various sites (Sections 3, pages 26-47). Shade and greening are mentioned with some proposed fabric and metal shade structures, but there is limited district-wide data or detailed strategies for campus greening or climate-adapted design.

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: The plan acknowledges safety and security concerns including exterior and interior safety measures (Section 3, pages 21-23), but does not provide a detailed climate risk assessment or comprehensive climate resilience strategies. Climate readiness is not a central theme.

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: The plan mentions some energy-related improvements such as new roofing with insulation, LED lighting, and HVAC upgrades (Section 3, pages 33-35). However, it lacks comprehensive data on energy use, detailed energy resilience strategies, or references to state requirements like Title 24 or Zero Net Energy goals.

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: The plan includes a funding options report and discusses bond funding and prioritization of projects (Section 6, pages 79-92). It provides some cost estimates and mentions funding sources but lacks detailed cost estimating methods, comprehensive prioritization criteria, or a long-term financial sustainability framework.
